title: Learning bass and the Gabriel trio in Prohibition
summary: He took bass lessons from Wendell McNeil, the rehearsal band never played a job, and the trio played from orchestrations, including Three Little Boys in a speakeasy.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, so then I had to learn something about the bass. So I went on to a fellow, he was, at one time, he was a good violin player, you might have heard of him, Wendell McNeil. Oh yes. Well I'd taken bass lessons onto him. He was playing bass at that time. I stayed with him about a year. Then I went out for myself and practiced, from what little I knew about music, from the trombone. Yeah. And that's how I came along. And with him and his brother, we used to practice, like I said, with that trio. The Gabriel trio. All in that time, you see. And fooling with this other band at the same time. And I was like, I'm a good guy. So then when we got together fully after this band broke up, they never did succeed. And all they did was the hoisting. Never played one job during the whole time. He was the hoisting. I'd say maybe a year or so. Just the hoisting.
Is the trombone the player the leader? No, the trumpet player.
Oh, the trumpet player. He was the trumpet player.

Oh yeah. Gus Eli Show. Oh yeah. Well, he never did. The only band he ever played in was this. Big military. Military band there. So that's when we got this, went on with this trio. And we did very well. We used to play music. Take orchestration and give him the banjo part. My brother and I would take the clarinet. And we used to play an orchestration with those three pieces from top to bottom. Is that right, Clarence? Yeah. That's really right. Oh, wow. And when Three Little Boys came out, we were playing in a speakeasy back on Computer Street. That was during Prohibition time. When Three Little Boys came out. We didn't buy that. We just picked it up and played it. And then Gus used to say, you say, you sound just like the fella playing on the record with Duke Ellington. I was playing the same thing. I was playing the same part. After we played it a while, then we bought the orchestration.
